correctness.rationale: For real q>1 and 0<z<1/2, boundary flow signs exclude boundary equilibria; all equilibria are interior. Dividing stationary equations yields ratio r=(x+z)/(y+z) with x/y=q²r²; exhaustive rational parametrization uses D=q²r³+(q²+q)r²-(q+1)r-1 and positive branches r in (0,q^-2) or (1,infinity). On the latter branch Z(r) strictly decreases from 1/2 to 0. On low-quality branch t=q²r in (0,1), Phi=q²t(1-t)/H and Phi_prime=q²G/H², with G(0)>0, G(1)<0 and G_prime<0 for q>1; hence exactly one nondegenerate maximum z*(q). Independently SymPy-reduced the derivative and Jacobian/ratio rational identities to zero; q=2 root t*=0.464372607811233 yields z*=0.049306126020888. Jacobian has negative trace at any equilibrium, and det=-(q²r²-1)E(r)/D², giving stable high branch, stable lower-r inferior branch and saddle upper-r inferior branch, and precisely one zero eigenvalue at fold. Denominator monotonicity in q proves strict threshold decrease and the sharp limits 1/5 and q² z*->1/4. These are local ODE equilibria, not stochastic/global fate claims.

value.rationale: The source model directly asks when inferior-option local consensus survives stubborn zealots despite quality advantage. Determining a unique, all-real-q algebraic threshold, branch stability and decay as q^-2 replaces a qualitative fold plot with a complete falsifiable bifurcation classification useful for model calibration. It is mathematical structure rather than merely retabulating plotted parameter values. It does not establish global basins, optimal policy, or random finite-swarm switching time.
